centralClaim: Claude conversations that users had shared by link were indexed by Google Search, making them findable by anyone rather than only by the people holding the link.

corroboration.quote: Google Search indexed public Claude AI chat links, letting people find shared conversations through the site query before those listings disappeared soon after.
Search engines briefly indexed shared Claude conversations, making them visible to anyone.

sendTest: If you ever hit Share on a Claude chat, it became a public web page. People found them on Google. Taking them off Google did not close them.
caption:
If you ever pressed Share on a Claude chat, that chat has been a public web page ever since.

Over the weekend a Reddit thread showed that a plain Google query, site:claude.ai/share, listed those pages. People who had never been sent a link could open them and read the conversation. Reports described legal discussions, source code and business files among them. Some users said they also found credentials and cryptocurrency information, and those particular finds have not been independently confirmed.

The results have since gone from Google. That is the part worth reading twice, because it changed nothing about the chats themselves. A share link stays live until the person who made it turns the conversation back to Private, and anyone who already saved the address can keep opening it.

Anthropic says it hands search engines no directory of shared conversations and blocks crawlers from its site. Spokesperson Gabby Curtis put earlier search visibility down to people posting their own links in public, where a search engine could find them.

Where to look: Settings, then Privacy, then Shared Chats.

Have you ever shared a chat and then forgotten it was still up?

slides.title: Where to look, tonight
slides.body: Open **Settings, Privacy, Shared Chats**. Anything holding personal data, work files, credentials or legal material goes back to *Private*. A copy someone already saved cannot be pulled back.
slides.evidence: Claude users can review active public links under Settings, Privacy and Shared Chats. Any conversation containing personal data, company information, credentials, legal material, or private code should be changed back to Private.
